title: Three witnesses will see the plates by faith
setting: Joseph Smith finished translating the Book of Mormon at Fayette, New York, in June 1829. The translation said three witnesses would see the plates and testify of them. Oliver Cowdery, David Whitmer, and Martin Harris each wanted to be one of them. Joseph inquired through the Urim and Thummim, and this revelation was the answer. Joseph later said that not many days after, the four men went into the woods to pray for the promised view. The earliest surviving copy dates from no earlier than late 1834 and may have been edited.
summary: The revelation tells the three men to rely on the Lord’s word with full purpose of heart. If they do, they will see the plates, breastplate, sword of Laban, Urim and Thummim, and Lehi’s directors. It says they will see these things by faith, like the prophets of old. Afterward they must testify of them by the power of God. Their testimony will help keep Joseph Smith from being destroyed. They will testify that they have seen as Joseph has seen. The voice declares that the translated book is true. If they obey, the gates of hell will not prevail against them.

contextNote.title: Seeing is tied to testifying
contextNote.text: Joseph had seen the plates alone, which left him exposed to doubt and attack. Verse 3 states the purpose of the view: after seeing, the three must testify by God’s power. Verse 4 gives the reason, that Joseph “may not be destroyed,” so God’s purposes go forward. Verse 1 had set the condition, relying on the Lord’s word with full purpose of heart. So the sight was not a reward for curiosity but a burden of witness. In this passage, to “testify” means to share responsibility for the claim Joseph had carried alone.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 12–17 connects this revelation to the Testimony of Three Witnesses printed in the Book of Mormon. Verses 2 and 5 both tie the witnesses’ sight to faith; why might the Lord have required faith before giving physical evidence?
reviewNote: Read all 9 verses. Official heading gives Fayette, June 1829, to Cowdery, Whitmer, and Harris, before they viewed the plates. JSP historical introduction read: dictated after translation was finished; Book of Mormon promises of three witnesses (Ether 5, 2 Nephi 27); earliest copy is Revelation Book 2 (F. G. Williams, after 25 Nov 1834); omitted from the Book of Commandments. The brother of Jared, Lehi, and the Red Sea are named in verse 1 but were not added as people or places. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes.
